defects: Conclusion asserts f is bounded everywhere on all of ℍ (∃ B, ∀ τ, |f τ| ≤ B) rather than bounded at the cusp i∞ (IsBoundedAtImInfty, i.e. bounded only as Im τ → ∞). This is a strictly stronger and in general false claim: e.g. h=1, c_m=1 for all m gives f(τ)=1/(1-q(τ)) with q(τ)=exp(2πiτ), which satisfies the q-expansion hypothesis (radius of convergence 1) but is unbounded as τ→0, so the produced statement is not even true, let alone equivalent to the gold.

Hypothesis is phrased as a tsum equality (∑' m, c m * q^m = f τ) rather than gold's HasSum hypothesis; tsum defaults to 0 when the series is not summable, so this does not genuinely assert convergence of the q-expansion, weakening the intended 'convergent q-expansion' hypothesis from the informal statement.
